Based on my search, here is information about **Medi-Cal**:

## What is Medi-Cal?

**Medi-Cal** is California's Medicaid program — a public health insurance program that provides free or low-cost medical services to eligible California residents. It is administered by the California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS).

## Key Features

- **Coverage**: Includes doctor visits, hospital care, prescription drugs, preventive services, mental health care, dental care (for children and some adults), vision care, and more
- **Expansion**: Under the Affordable Care Act, California expanded Medi-Cal eligibility to include more low-income adults without dependent children
- **Enrollment**: Serves over 15 million Californians (roughly 1 in 3 residents), making it one of the largest Medicaid programs in the United States
- **Managed Care**: Most beneficiaries receive services through managed care plans

## Eligibility

Eligibility is based on factors including:
- Income level (generally up to 138% of the federal poverty level for adults)
- Family size
- Age (children, seniors 65+)
- Disability status
- Pregnancy
- Immigration status (with some limitations)

## How to Apply

- **Online**: Through [Covered California](https://www.coveredca.com) or [BenefitsCal](https://www.benefitscal.com)
- **Phone**: Contact your county social services office
- **In-person**: At county human services agencies

## Recent Developments

California has been expanding Medi-Cal coverage, including initiatives to cover undocumented immigrants of all ages (full expansion completed in January 2024) and adding new benefits like food and housing supports through "CalAIM" (California Advancing and Innovating Medi-Cal).

3. https://www.benefitscal.com
4. https://www.medicaid.gov/medicaid/by-state/california/index.html
5. https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/calaim
